Ven was one of the earliest believers that we could use our then-current model to solve millenium prize problems.

There are a lot of brilliant people in the world, but being brilliant and also having correctly-placed confidence and courage to keep pushing on something that others don't think is possible is a very valuable thing and fairly rare.

I am grateful so many people at OpenAI have this combination.

Oh, one thing about kids:

Most good things get a little less satisfying the 100th time you do them.

A quiet evening hanging out with your kids, even doing very mundane stuff, is in the rare category of something repetitive just getting better and better.

I am thankful for a lot of things in life, but my family is the best thing that has ever happened to me.

The two most common things people said to me before having kids is that it's better than anyone can explain to you and it goes very fast; these are both true and I don't have much to add. But I am very grateful and I love them more than there is any way to explain.

Also I cannot really imagine life without Ollie and I think without his unwavering support and great advice I would have gone crazy by now.

🦃
I don't think I'd heard the word "hyperstitioning" before, but it's a good one.

We’re now testing Private Inference, our latest offering as part of OpenAI Private Intelligence, with a small group of customers.

Stronger privacy protections will make frontier AI useful for a lot more work, and business privacy is important for a healthy ecosystem. Reach out to @shekar4x if interested!

(Also, ZDR with Private Safety Processing enables automated safety reviews without giving OpenAI personnel access to the underlying content.)

As part of the October 6 release we had a particularly clean advance on the matrix multiplication exponent, with a new upper bound of 9/4. Since then, the model has been working on a LOWER BOUND for this exponent. This is already pretty crazy since NOTHING was known for lower bounds! Today we announced that actually 9/4 is tight ... This is really the kind of result that I never thought I would see in my lifetime.

(btw, by an "old" result of Yin Tat Lee and collaborators this also implies that linear programs can be solved in time n^{9/4}.)

Labs agreed under the White House Accords to establish standards and best practices to improve the safety of their systems, and I believe a discussion about the use of perplexity can further these goals.
